title: Why Bilge Water Forced Sailors to Drink Rum
hook: Fresh water turned into green slime within two weeks at sea.

scenes.text: On long sea voyages, fresh drinking water was stored in large wooden oak casks deep in the dark, warm ship hold.
scenes.imagePrompt: Deep cargo hold of a wooden sailing ship stacked high with massive iron-hooped wooden oak water casks. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: On long sea voyages, fresh drinking water was stored in large wooden oak casks deep in the dark, warm ship hold.

scenes.text: Within two weeks in tropical Caribbean heat, the water turned foul, growing thick green algae and crawling with mosquito larvae.
scenes.imagePrompt: Murky green liquid inside a wooden bucket with slimy algae edges under dim candlelight. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Within two weeks in tropical Caribbean heat, the water turned foul, growing thick green algae and crawling with mosquito larvae.

scenes.text: To make putrid water drinkable and kill deadly bacteria, sailors mixed it with potent high-proof Caribbean sugar cane rum.
scenes.imagePrompt: Wooden ship table with brown glass rum bottle, copper measuring funnel, and sliced sour limes. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: To make putrid water drinkable and kill deadly bacteria, sailors mixed it with potent high-proof Caribbean sugar cane rum.

scenes.text: In 1740, British Admiral Edward Vernon ordered the mixture diluted with water and lime juice, creating the legendary cocktail called 'Grog'.
scenes.imagePrompt: Heavy wooden grog tub embossed with brass lettering 'The King God Bless Him' and copper serving dippers on deck. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: In 1740, British Admiral Edward Vernon ordered the mixture diluted with water and lime juice, creating the legendary cocktail called 'Grog'.

scenes.text: The added lime juice accidentally cured scurvy, while the alcohol kept crews hydrated without dying of cholera or dysentery.

scenes.voicedText: The added lime juice accidentally cured scurvy, while the alcohol kept crews hydrated without dying of cholera or dysentery.
